entry.title: Damages Calculator — Raytracing Public Funds
entry.content:
$46.1 Million in Public Funds. Seven Raytraces. Twenty Public Officials.

In computer graphics, raytracing works by shooting a ray from the observer’s eye backward through every surface it bounced off until you find the light source. This is the same technique applied to public money.

Start at the student. Trace backward through every membrane. Find the emitter.

Data source: /api/damages.json — machine-readable, independently verifiable.

Membranes crossed: 5 (law firm → entity formation → dark money → election → board seat → oversight) Funds traced: $84,000 in SDJ election spending Damage: Dark money elected the board member who oversees the convicted felon’s school.

Ray 7: Total System Capture (The Dykema Recursion)

Start: Dykema. End: Dykema. It’s the same node at every level.

Membranes crossed: 0 There are no membranes. One firm operates every level of the system simultaneously. The law, the defense of the law, the entities created under the law, and the elections that control who oversees the entities created under the law — all route through the same Lansing office.

How to Read This Calculator

Each ray starts at the damage point (student, taxpayer, public trust) and traces backward through every membrane (authorization, election, appointment, judicial decision) until it reaches the emitter (the person or entity that generated the ray).

In computer graphics, when a ray passes through too many surfaces without finding a light source, it dies. In this system, every ray finds its source. The system is fully traced.

A membrane is any institutional boundary that should prevent a signal from passing — a firewall between the regulator and the regulated, between the judge and the litigant, between the law firm and the entity it formed. When a ray passes through a membrane it should have been stopped by, that membrane is breached.

When the ray starts and ends at the same node (Ray 7), there are no membranes at all. The system has achieved total capture — the entity that wrote the rules also operates within them, defends them, forms entities under them, and controls who enforces them.
